b2-cuba-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Unfortunately, Old Havana
b2-cuba-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Old Havana, and he asks what you thought about the state of the buildings.
b2-cuba-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what the documentary said about the buildings, with your own reaction.
cues: Say that some buildings are in poor condition
Show that you think it is a pity
b2-cuba-01.target: Lamentablemente, algunos edificios de La Habana Vieja están en mal estado.
b2-cuba-01.english: Unfortunately, some buildings in Old Havana are in poor condition.
b2-cuba-01.canDo: I can show my attitude to a fact with stance adverbs such as *lamentablemente*, *francamente* and *en rigor*.

b2-cuba-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Martí Wrote
b2-cuba-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about José Martí, and she asks what he wanted for Cuba.
b2-cuba-02.prompt: Tell Meg what Martí wrote he wanted.
cues: Say that he wanted the independence of Cuba
b2-cuba-02.target: Martí escribió que quería la independencia de Cuba.
b2-cuba-02.english: Martí wrote that he wanted the independence of Cuba.
b2-cuba-02.canDo: I can report what someone said or wrote, shifting the tenses (*quería*, *había escrito*, *haría*).

b2-cuba-03.title: Communicative Challenge: If Necessary, They Stayed
b2-cuba-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the literacy campaign of 1961, and he asks what the young teachers did when it got late.
b2-cuba-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the volunteer teachers did if it was necessary.
cues: Start with a condition without si
Say that they stayed to sleep at the family's house
b2-cuba-03.target: De ser necesario, los brigadistas se quedaban a dormir en la casa de la familia.
b2-cuba-03.english: If necessary, the volunteer teachers stayed to sleep in the family's house.
b2-cuba-03.canDo: I can state a condition without *si*, with *de* + infinitive or the gerund.

b2-cuba-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Meeting a Troubadour
b2-cuba-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are listening to a talk about the Nueva Trova, and she asks whether you had heard that music before.
b2-cuba-04.prompt: Tell Meg when you first got to know the son, and what you did not know then.
cues: Say that you got to know the son
Say that you did not know where it was born
b2-cuba-04.target: Cuando conocí el son, no sabía que había nacido en el este de la isla.
b2-cuba-04.english: When I got to know the son, I did not know it had been born in the east of the island.
b2-cuba-04.canDo: I can tell the difference between *conocí* and *conocía*, *supe* and *sabía*, *quise* and *quería*, *pude* and *podía*.

b2-cuba-05.title: Communicative Challenge: However Much They Open Up
b2-cuba-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about Cuba in the 1990s, and he asks what the text says about tourism.
b2-cuba-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened in the 1990s even though Cuba opened to tourism.
cues: Say that Cuba opened to tourism
Say that the years stayed difficult
b2-cuba-05.target: Por más que se abrió al turismo, el país siguió pasando años difíciles.
b2-cuba-05.english: However much it opened to tourism, the country went on through difficult years.
b2-cuba-05.canDo: I can say that nothing changes however much something happens, with *por más que* and *por mucho que*.

b2-cuba-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Cuba in Review
b2-cuba-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about Cuba, and you want to give her one example of what you will say about Havana.
b2-cuba-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what you think about the state of some buildings in Old Havana.
cues: Show that you think it is a pity
Say that some buildings are in poor condition
b2-cuba-consolidation.target: Lamentablemente, algunos edificios de La Habana Vieja están en mal estado.
b2-cuba-consolidation.english: Unfortunately, some buildings in Old Havana are in poor condition.
b2-cuba-consolidation.canDo: I can show my attitude to a fact with stance adverbs such as *lamentablemente* and *en rigor*.
